newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanbo Steel defaults payments on notes.
newsitem.headline: Hanbo Steel defaults payments on notes.

text.p: Hanbo Steel Corp, a unit of South Korea's Hanbo Group, was not able to honour payments on an unspecified amount of promissory notes on Thursday, officials at the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute said.
The company was saddled with about 5.7 trillion won worth of debt as a result of excessive facilities expansion, Hanbo Steel officials have said.
"It is true Hanbo defaulted on loan payments today," said an official. But he declined to give details.
Domestic Yonhap TV reported Hanbo failed to pay 1.5 billion won worth of notes to Boram Bank.
Hanbo said chairman Chung Tae-soo and his family agreed to hand over four million shares to four creditor banks and abandon all rights attached to them.
"But it does not mean the chairman gave up managerial rights to the company," Hanbo spokesman Kim Kye-hong said.
Creditor banks have said rescue loans would be made to Hanbo if Chung abandoned the company's management.
Officials at creditor banks, including the Korea First Bank, earlier said a takeover was being sought for the troubled company.
Hanbo's three other creditors include the Korea Development Bank, Chohung Bank and the Korea Exchange Bank.
Hanbo's debt problems stem from the construction of a steel mill in the southeastern city of Tangjin, analysts said.
They said construction has so far cost 4.96 trillion won and an additional 750 billion won would be needed for completion.
